$comment: Modules follow docs/RESEARCH.md 9.2 item 9 and 7.3. `unlock` names the module that must be finished first (the tutorial completed, or every principle of that module at >= moduleUnlockStars mastery stars from elo.mastery). Level `unlockStars` is the minimum stars on every principle of a module before that level opens. All numbers here are tunable design defaults [D] drawn from RESEARCH 7.1 and 7.3: level 3 at 3 stars mirrors 'timer only after untimed accuracy of about 0.80' (7.1 row 10); session.blockSize is the 8-12 blocked items of 7.1 row 8; session.mix and probeEvery are 7.3. `scenarios` lists scenario IDs in play order and is filled in as scenarios are authored.

description.standard: One principle at a time: watch a worked example, finish a half-placed scene, then place yourself freely, with no clock.
description.kid: One idea at a time, with help and no clock.

description.standard: The module's principles are shuffled together, including look-alike situations, so you have to recognise which idea applies before you move.
description.kid: Mixed-up scenes: work out which idea you need.

description.standard: Live sequences against the clock: keep adjusting as play unfolds, first slowed down, then at full speed and faster.
description.kid: Live play against the clock: keep moving with the ball.

description.standard: Learn how the pitch is divided and which way you are playing, then the ideas every position depends on: your job around the ball, goal-side and the offside line.
description.kid: Learn the parts of the pitch, which way we go and a few key rules.

pitchChallenge.standard: Watch five minutes of any match and, each time the ball is passed, name the third and the lane it lands in.
pitchChallenge.kid: Watch a game and say which part of the pitch the ball is in.

modules.title: Pressure, cover and balance
modules.subtitle: Defending as a unit of three

description.standard: Out of possession every defender has one of three jobs: press the ball, cover the presser or balance the team. Learn to read which job is yours, how to recover when you are caught upfield and how to defend a cross.
description.kid: Learn the three defending jobs: press the ball, back up, or hold the shape.

focus.standard: One job at a time: press the carrier, then cover the presser at an angle, then tuck in on the far side.
focus.kid: Practise one defending job at a time.

focus.standard: Mixed scenes where you first decide whether you are the first, second or third defender, including recovery runs and crosses.
focus.kid: Mixed scenes: work out your job first.

focus.standard: Live play: keep adjusting as the ball moves and your job switches between pressing, covering and balancing.
focus.kid: Live play: keep moving as your job changes.

label.kid: Go to the ball or back off?

pitchChallenge.standard: In your next game, every time the other team wins the ball, decide in one second whether you are pressing, covering or balancing, then do that job.
pitchChallenge.kid: Next game: when they get the ball, ask yourself: press, back up, or tuck in?

modules.title: Support, width and depth
modules.subtitle: Helping the player on the ball

description.standard: In possession, where you stand decides whether the carrier has options. Learn to offer a clear passing lane at the right distance, stretch the pitch with width and depth, and find the half-spaces and the gaps between their lines.
description.kid: Learn where to stand so your teammate on the ball can pass to you.

focus.standard: One idea at a time: open a passing lane, then hold the width, then pin their back line.
focus.kid: Practise one way of helping at a time.

focus.standard: Mixed scenes where you choose between coming short and staying away, and between holding the width and moving inside.
focus.kid: Mixed scenes: come close, or stay wide and far?

focus.standard: Live build-up: keep offering the right option as the ball moves up the pitch and into their box.
focus.kid: Live play: keep getting free as the ball moves.

label.standard: Show for the ball or stay on the last defender?
Hold the width or tuck in?

pitchChallenge.standard: Next time your team has the ball, check before each pass: does the player on the ball have two open options, and are you one of them?
pitchChallenge.kid: Next game: when a teammate has the ball, make sure they can pass to you.

description.standard: Good teams defend as one compact block. Learn to keep the lines close, hold a level back line, step up or drop at the right moment, and play your part as a centre-back, full-back or #6.
description.kid: Learn to move with your teammates as one tight group.

focus.standard: One idea at a time: stay compact, keep a level line, then step up or drop with the ball.
focus.kid: Practise one team-shape idea at a time.

focus.standard: Mixed scenes: step up or hold, crescent or L-shape, high block or low block.
focus.kid: Mixed scenes: step up, stay, or drop?

focus.standard: Live defending: keep the whole block together through a full passage of play.
focus.kid: Live play: move as one group the whole time.

label.standard: Step up or hold the line?
label.kid: Move up or stay in line?

pitchChallenge.standard: Watch a match and pause when the ball goes wide: is the back four level, and are the gaps between the defenders about 12 m or less?
pitchChallenge.kid: Watch a game: when the ball goes wide, do the defenders stay in a line?
